# Working in this repository

Bookish is a spoiler-aware character-chart site for fantasy series. Three charts
share one schema, one rendering engine, and one spoiler gate.

## The one rule that matters

**Every read of series data goes through `gate()` in `src/spoiler.ts`.**

Do not filter by reading position anywhere else. A second implementation is a
second chance to get it wrong, and the failure mode is spoiling someone's book.
The chart renderer, the ask box, the MCP server and the eval harness all call it.

## Before changing data

`data/*.json` is the source of truth. It is generated by
`scripts/extract-charts.mjs` from `sources/`, and every transformation applied to
it carries a `why`. Do not hand-edit `data/` — add a correction to the extractor
so the reasoning survives.

Read these before touching the shape of anything:

- `DATA-DICTIONARY.md` — every field, and which chart's design won each argument
- `RELATIONSHIPS.md` — the canonical 14 relationship types and their directions
- `DATA-MODEL.md` — why state is stored per book

Two mechanisms are easy to confuse:

- **`changes[]`** — the world changed. Jack really does become venin.
- **`perceived`** — the reader was wrong. Brennan was alive the whole time.

If the earlier value was never true, it is `perceived`, not a change.

## Conventions

- Book numbers start at 1.
- Character ids are lowercase slugs, never display names.
- Relationship direction carries meaning: for `killed`, `from` is the killer;
  for `family`, `to` is `from`'s label.
- `npm run validate` must pass. Warnings fail the build too — that is deliberate,
  and there is a ratchet comment in `scripts/validate.ts` explaining why.
- Tests assert that validators **reject** bad input. A test that only accepts
  good input proves nothing.

## What an agent may not do

See `AUTONOMY.md`. In short: propose on a branch, never merge, never edit the
schema or the vocabulary, never resolve a canon question — surface it instead.
